hints: Look closely at X and notice it is not an open chain ester, it is a cyclic ester called a lactone.
Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the acyl-oxygen bond, so the ring O stays with the alkyl chain as an alcohol and the C=O becomes a carboxylate.
Check where the methyl group ends up and remember heating with NaOH(aq) gives the $\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ salt, not the free $\text{-COOH}$ acid.
walkthrough:
**Identify X as a lactone**

Think of X as an internal ester. The five-membered ring contains $-\text{COO}-$ where the C=O is joined back to the alkyl chain through O.

$$\text{cyclic ester (lactone) + NaOH(aq) } \rightarrow \text{ hydroxy carboxylate salt}$$

**Open the ring by alkaline hydrolysis**

Ester hydrolysis with hot aqueous NaOH always cleaves the C(=O)-O bond. Add $\text{OH}^-$ to the carbonyl carbon and H to the ring oxygen in effect.

$$\text{RCOOR' + NaOH } \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{R'OH}$$

**Draw the correct hydroxy carboxylate**

The ring O was attached to the carbon bearing the $\text{CH}_3$ group, so that carbon becomes $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-}$. The carbonyl carbon becomes $\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$.

$$\text{HO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$$

**Choose the matching structure**

This is a 4-hydroxy pentanoate salt with a secondary alcohol on the left and a sodium carboxylate on the right. That matches only one of the four options.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows $\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$, a primary alcohol with the methyl on the middle carbon. The ring O in X is on the methyl-bearing carbon, so hydrolysis must give a secondary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-}$, not $\text{HO-CH}_2$-.
options.B: Incorrect for two reasons. It has the wrong carbon skeleton like A (primary alcohol instead of secondary) and it shows a free carboxylic acid $\text{-COOH}$. Hot NaOH(aq) neutralises the acid to give the $\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ salt.
options.C: Correct. Ring opening at the acyl-oxygen bond gives $\text{HO-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$. This has the secondary alcohol on the methyl-bearing carbon and the sodium carboxylate from alkaline hydrolysis, exactly as shown.
options.D: Incorrect. The carbon skeleton with the secondary alcohol $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-}$ is right, but it shows $\text{-COOH}$ instead of $\text{-COO}^-\text{Na}^+$. Acid hydrolysis with dilute HCl would give this hydroxy acid, but NaOH(aq) gives the salt.
